ChemTec Publishing Databook of UV Stabilizers, 3rd Edition/Copyrights 2025; ChemTec Publishing 1 Introduction Polymeric materials used outdoors require protection against UV radiation, temperature, pollutants, and moisture. Their combined action causes changes commonly known as weathering changes. In most cases, these changes occur after only a brief exposure of products to degrading elements of nature. Some products, such as cosmetics, are designed to protect the surface (skin) from degradation. For the above reasons, most formulations are incomplete without the addition of adequately selected stabilizers. The aim of this book is to show the properties of stabilizers which are added to materials to protect them from weathering changes. In the title of the book, they are called by a common name of UV stabilizers, but the stabilizers may have diff erent func- tions in material protection. They are frequently added in combination, sometimes because all their various functions are necessary for the protection of particular materials or because together they enhance actions of each other  a phenomenon commonly kn in combination, sometimes because all their various functions are necessary for the protection of particular materials or because together they enhance actions of each other  a phenomenon commonly known as syner- gism. Commercial products which are included in this selection are in the common use and characteristic of the group discussed. There are some similar products from diff erent manu- facturers, which are included in this book for comparison of their properties. Many similar products available in the market were also not presented to limit repetitions. The following groups of materials used as stabilizers are included in the book: organic UV absorbers (15 chemical groups) inorganic UV absorbers (or screeners) fi bers hindered amine stabilizers (monomeric, oligomeric, and polymeric) phenolic antioxidants phosphites and phosphonites thiosynergists amines quenchers optical brighteners synergistic combinations of the above stabilizers (7 groups given as examples) The individual stabilizers are discussed in the form of tables, which include the following information: general physical-chemical properties eff ect on health and safety eff ect on the environment use and practical applications Each of the measurable factors of materials essential for the above groups is characterized in the next chapter. The theory behind UV degradation and stabilization can be found in two recently published books: Handbook of Materials Weathering, 7th Edition and Handbook of UV Degradation and Stabilization, 3rd Edition.
